analysis.hypothesis: Implement BatchNorm2d eval-mode elementwise normalization as a CUDA kernel in kernels/custom_ops.cu. Use a 1D kernel over total elements with per-element channel index computed from strides, handling arbitrary x strides. Weight/bias/running_mean/running_var are contiguous C-length arrays. Output uses same shape/strides as x. Launcher signature: norm_forward_launcher(const float* x, float* out, const float* weight, const float* bias, const float* running_mean, const float* running_var, float eps, int64_t N, int64_t C, int64_t H, int64_t W, const int64_t* x_sizes, const int64_t* x_strides, cudaStream_t stream).
evidence: Contract specifies elementwise per-channel formula y = (x - running_mean[c]) / sqrt(running_var[c] + eps) * weight[c] + bias[c].
Reference model uses BatchNorm2d in eval mode with running stats; no reduction needed.
Input shape [32,3,256,512], float32 CUDA; output same shape/dtype/device.
Binding fragments indicate C++ wrapper will pass optional tensors as pointers (or nullptr) and will ensure contiguous for 1D tensors, but x may be non-contiguous; kernel must handle general strides.
changes: Write kernels/custom_ops.cu containing a __global__ kernel norm_forward_kernel that iterates over all elements using grid-stride loop, computes channel index from N,C,H,W and x_strides, and applies affine normalization.
Provide extern "C" launcher norm_forward_launcher with the exact signature expected by binding stage.
No convolutions needed; only elementwise kernel.
Ensure thread safety: no memory writes beyond output size; output can alias input? Contract separate output allocation; binding will allocate torch::empty_like(x) so no aliasing issue.
Grid-stride loop handles arbitrary total elements; block size 256.
